title: Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Fairer Rules for General Treatments) Bill 2019
short_title: Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Fairer Rules for General Treatments) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would stop private health insurers from paying different rebates for the same treatment under the same product in the same state or territory.
It would let the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority step in when insurers misuse data from the Health Industry Claims and Payments Service to distort competition.
The bill would also ban health funds from acting as both insurers and providers of general health treatments.
changes: Prevents private health insurers from offering different rebates for identical treatments under the same product in the same jurisdiction.
Gives the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority power to intervene if insurers improperly use HICAPS data to manipulate the market.
Bans private health funds from being both insurers and providers of general health treatments.
summary.affected: Private health insurers, the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority, and the Health Industry Claims and Payments Service.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wilkie
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment (Fairer Rules for General Treatments) Bill 2019 is needed to address the private health insurance sector's decline, citing 65,000 fewer Australians with coverage in December 2018—the largest drop in 15 years—and the AMA president's warning that the sector is "on the precipice." The bill would prohibit differential rebates, prevent insurers from owning medical clinics, and regulate insurers' use of HICAPS data, following the 2017 Senate committee recommendation 12.
